parties:
Shahin and others
Vs.
The State
full_judgment:
17. The statement of prosecutrix if believed then conviction can be given solely relying on that. Trial Court on this settled principle of law convicted the appellants. But on consideration of the following facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record we hold that the testimony of the prosecutrix in the present case before us cannot be believed:-(a) P.W.1 (the informant), P.W.2 (victim), P.W.3, P.W.6 (Investigating Officer) their depositions clearly suggested enmity with the appellant Shahin and for which a doubt is created that there might be a strong possibility that at the behest of the inimical quarter of the appellants they Were implicated in the case when admittedly from the evidence on record it is found that there was a feud concerning a 'Gher between the appellant Shahin and one Khokan Sarder. If these statements of P.Ws. 1-3 and P.W.6 (I.0.) together with the fact that this victim was married twice and also that arrest of the appellant took place right after the occurrence on 6.10.96 are taken into consideration the only irresistible inference which could be made is that the instant case might be a planted one and also it can be inferred that the testimony of the prosecutrix is bereft of truth, blended with falsehood which can be viewed with suspicion and doubt. (b) Next comes another aspect. Medical certificate followed by a test of the victim was issued on 6.10.96 right after the occurrence that took place on 5.10.96. It is proved by P.W.6 (Doctor). Medical certificate says "No sign of rape found" —So immediately after the occurrence of rape, as alleged, when admittedly from the evidence of the victim it is revealed that there was a scuffle i.e. resistance from the victim and that she also stated that the occurrence of rape continued for an hour, a natural presumption wells up why any mark of violence or any impact of rape is absent ? The decision of Abu Taher Vs. State 6 MLR (AD) 77 though says when medical certificate does not suggest any sign of rape found in the body of the victim, it does not get preference over other evidence since it is merely an opinion. But in that 6 MLR case the victim was examined after 7 days. But in. the present case the victim was examined immediately after the occurrence i.e. the following day on 6.10.96. (c) Next we see that the trial Court did not notice the vital aspect that the medical certificate was given on 6.10.96 though signed on 9.10.96. Thus, it came to an erroneous finding that since after 4 days medical certificate was given the sign of rape could not be found. (d) Let us now digress to another side of the case. Mr. Justice Md. Hassan Ameen in the case of Hossain Shially (Fakir) Vs. State — reported in 56 DLR 637 held that: "In a case of allegation of rape where there is no independent eye-witness and t the only evidence is that of the prosecutrix herself and of those to whom it was reported, the Courts are not left with any objective test of gauging the truth of story of the prosecutirx. " Further in this context his Lordship placed reliance on the decision of Momataz Ahmed Vs. State-reported in 19 DLR (SC) 259 which held: "The evidence of a prosecutrix in a rape case customarily, being a woman of full age, is not accepted as sufficient, but requires corroboration by independent evidence in order to be believed". This decision was delivered by his Lordship Justice Cornelias. In another case of Md. Abdul Khaleque and others Vs. State-reported in 12 DLR (SC) 165. Justice Cornelias elaborating this aspect of criminal jurisprudence again observed: 

 20. The statements made by the victim under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, her deposition before the Court, deposition of P.Ws. 2 and 3 and P.W. 6 (Investigating Officer) if critically scrutinized and assessed it gives a clear rise to a presumption of innocence of the accused-appellants. The chain of circumstances in the present case as discussed above inevitably, irresistibly and certainly suggest that all these facts can be linked up not with the guilt but with the innocence of the accused-appellants. Therefore, the instant case before us is indeed an exception of the general rule of law that if the sole testimony of the prosecutrix inspires confidence or it is credit worthy, conviction can be given solely upon that. On the other hand this case is an example where, for the reasons stated above the sole testimony of the prosecutrix cannot be given credence and thus cannot' be relied in awarding punishment believing the same.
